notes:
Auto-designed from: Design an Ob3ect for:

A symmetric informationally complete positive-operator-valued measure in dimension d: a frame of

phase_0.boundary_condition: the d-dimensional Hilbert space, the traceless Hermitian operator space, and the d^2-point simplex centered on the maximally mixed state
phase_0.domain_name: A symmetric informationally complete positive-operator-valued measure in dimension d:
phase_0.justification: Auto-designed by the native Ob3ect Auto-Designer (in-process candle, no Python)

AFWD.justification: the fiducial vector forms a rank-one projector, and verified projectors map to simplex points centered on the maximally mixed state

AREV.justification: projectors descend to centered simplex coordinates, and orbit equations descend to fiducial component polynomials

CLINK.justification: successive clock and shift operators compose to produce the d^2 projectors from one fiducial vector

ENGAGR.justification: solved dimensions and unsolved dimensions are held live together as the open object without forcing a single resolution

EVALF.justification: negative arms record overlap deviations and polynomial obstructions

EVALT.chosen_element: constant overlap and solvable polynomial evidence
EVALT.justification: affirmative arms affirm constant overlap magnitudes and fiducial components satisfying the polynomial system

FFUSE.justification: the overlap arms rejoin into a candidate SIC-POVM state, and the polynomial arms rejoin into a dimension-specific closure state

FSPLIT.justification: the orbit opens into verified and rejected overlap arms, and the polynomial system opens into solvable and unsolvable arms

IFIX.chosen_element: fiducial, orbit, overlap, and polynomial ledger
IFIX.justification: the fiducial vector, generated orbit, overlap record, and polynomial equations are fixed in an append-only store

IMSCRIB.justification: the normalized fiducial vector is the self-referential seed that remains unchanged while its orbit is generated

TANCH.chosen_element: open polynomial frontier for all d
TANCH.justification: the terminal boundary contains the Hilbert space, the simplex, the orbit, and the unresolved existence problem as one object

VINIT.chosen_element: unassigned dimension d and empty fiducial vector
VINIT.justification: no projector, no overlap magnitude, and no polynomial constraint exist before the SIC-POVM construction begins

phase_2.fuse_result: one dimension-specific state carrying solution evidence or obstruction evidence
phase_2.rejoin_note: The overlap fork rejoins into a candidate state, the fixed-d closure fork rejoins into a dimension-specific state, and the all-d existence fork is left open.
phase_2.split_input: polynomial system in fiducial components for a fixed dimension
phase_2.verdict_reason: FSPLIT3 at step 5 dangles — no matching FFUSE3

phase_3.both_description: B4 B (11): both held at once, solved and unsolved dimensions remain live in the open frontier
phase_3.false_description: B4 F (10): constructively refuted, the fiducial orbit fails the constant overlap condition
phase_3.true_description: B4 T (01): constructively proven, a fiducial orbit satisfies the constant overlap condition
phase_3.void_description: B4 N (00): neither, no dimension, no fiducial vector, and no projector established

steps.domain_action: dimension d and fiducial vector are unassigned
the fiducial ray is identified with itself as the seed
the fiducial vector forms a rank-one projector
clock and shift operators compose into the Heisenberg-Weyl orbit
the orbit opens into a verified overlap arm and a rejected overlap arm
the verified arm checks that all overlap magnitudes equal 1/(d+1)
the verified projectors map to simplex points centered on the maximally mixed state
the rejected arm records overlap magnitudes that deviate from 1/(d+1)
the rejected projectors descend to traceless Hermitian coordinates
the verified and rejected arms rejoin into one candidate SIC-POVM state
the fiducial vector, orbit, and overlap record are appended to the permanent ledger
the orbit equations reduce to a polynomial system in the fiducial components
the all-d existence problem opens into a fixed-d closure arm and an open frontier arm
the fixed-d closure arm opens into a solvable arm and an unsolvable arm
the solvable arm produces fiducial components satisfying the polynomial system
the unsolvable arm records an obstruction for that dimension
the fixed-d closure arm rejoins into a dimension-specific closure state
the open frontier arm records dimensions where no closure is established
the solved and unsolved dimensions are held together as the open object
the open polynomial frontier is anchored as the terminal object

phase_5.alfs_store: the canonical reference store of known SIC-POVM fiducial vectors, Heisenberg-Weyl group tables, and the polynomial frontier for each dimension
phase_5.compiler_frontend: translates a chosen dimension d and fiducial vector into clock-and-shift operators, projectors, overlap equations, and polynomial constraints
phase_5.ipc_mechanism: passes fiducial components, orbit indices, projector matrices, overlap magnitudes, and simplex coordinates between construction, verification, and reduction stages
phase_5.memory_mechanism: stores fiducial vectors, generated projectors, traceless Hermitian coordinates, and polynomial equations in an append-only ledger
phase_5.scheduler_mechanism: orders dimension selection, fiducial initialization, orbit generation, overlap evaluation, polynomial reduction, and frontier update

phase_6.cycle_cost: one fiducial vector, d^2 orbit operations, d^2(d^2-1)/2 overlap checks, and one polynomial reduction per cycle
phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS ≈ 0: the cycle conserves information by moving the same fiducial data from vector form to orbit, overlap, and polynomial form without discarding evidence
phase_6.post_cycle_state: a recorded fiducial orbit, overlap evidence, and an updated polynomial frontier
phase_6.pre_cycle_state: an unassigned dimension and empty fiducial state
